   Description                         Active Sessions      Recommendations
                                       Percent of Activity
   ----------------------------------  -------------------  ---------------

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~


          Findings and Recommendations
          ----------------------------

Finding 1: Session Connect and Disconnect
Impact is 8.72 active sessions, 43.31% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
Session connect and disconnect calls were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 8.71 active sessions, 43.31% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic for possible reduction of connect and
      disconnect calls. For example, you might use a connection pool scheme in
      the middle tier.


Finding 2: Commits and Rollbacks
Impact is 7.92 active sessions, 39.35% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
Waits on event "log file sync" while performing COMMIT and ROLLBACK operations
were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Host Configuration
   Estimated benefit is 7.92 active sessions, 39.35% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the possibility of improving the performance of I/O to the
      online redo log files.
   Rationale
      The average size of writes to the online redo log files was 36 K and the
      average time per write was 1 milliseconds.
   Rationale
      The total I/O throughput on redo log files was 10 M per second for reads
      and 21 M per second for writes.
   Rationale
      The redo log I/O throughput was divided as follows: 0% by RMAN and
      recovery, 66% by Log Writer, 0% by Archiver, 0% by Streams AQ and 33% by
      all other activity.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Wait class "Commit" was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is 7.92 active sessions, 39.35% of total activity.


Finding 3: Undersized SGA
Impact is 2.47 active sessions, 12.26% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
The SGA was inadequately sized, causing additional I/O or hard parses.
The value of parameter "sga_target" was "143360 M" during the analysis period.

   Recommendation 1: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is .77 active sessions, 3.82% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Increase the size of the SGA by setting the parameter "sga_target" to
      152320 M.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Wait class "User I/O" was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is 4.7 active sessions, 23.38% of total activity.
      Hard parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is 1.38 active sessions, 6.88% of total activity.


Finding 4: Unusual "User I/O" Wait Event
Impact is 1.72 active sessions, 8.55% of total activity.
--------------------------------------------------------
Wait event "Disk file operations I/O" in wait class "User I/O" was consuming
significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.72 active sessions, 8.55% of total activity.
   -------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the cause for high "Disk file operations I/O" waits. Refer
      to Oracle's "Database Reference" for the description of this wait event.

   Recommendation 2: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.71 active sessions, 8.52% of total activity.
   -------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the cause for high "Disk file operations I/O" waits in
      Service "SYS$USERS".

   Recommendation 3: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.71 active sessions, 8.52% of total activity.
   -------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the cause for high "Disk file operations I/O" waits with
      P1,P2,P3 ("FileOperation, fileno, filetype") values "2", "0" and "15"
      respectively.

   Recommendation 4: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.71 active sessions, 8.51% of total activity.
   -------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the cause for high "Disk file operations I/O" waits in
      Module "oracle@ambaddb1".

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Wait class "User I/O" was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is 4.7 active sessions, 23.38% of total activity.


Finding 5: Soft Parse
Impact is 1.08 active sessions, 5.36% of total activity.
--------------------------------------------------------
Soft parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.08 active sessions, 5.36% of total activity.
   -------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic to keep open the frequently used cursors.
      Note that cursors are closed by both cursor close calls and session
      disconnects.

   Recommendation 2: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is 1.08 active sessions, 5.36% of total activity.
   -------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Consider increasing the session cursor cache size by increasing the
      value of parameter "session_cached_cursors".
   Rationale
      The value of parameter "session_cached_cursors" was "1000" during the
      analysis period.


Finding 6: Index Block Split
Impact is .71 active sessions, 3.5% of total activity.
------------------------------------------------------
Contention on index block splits was consuming significant database time.
However, no single index was the predominant cause for this contention.

   No recommendations are available.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Wait class "Concurrency" was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is 1.13 active sessions, 5.62% of total activity.


Finding 7: Hard Parse Due to Invalidations
Impact is .64 active sessions, 3.18% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
Cursors were getting invalidated due to DDL operations. This resulted in
additional hard parses which were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .64 active sessions, 3.18% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate appropriateness of DDL operations.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Hard parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is 1.38 active sessions, 6.88% of total activity.


Finding 8: Hard Parse Due to Sharing Criteria
Impact is .55 active sessions, 2.73% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
SQL statements with the same text were not shared because of cursor
environment mismatch. This resulted in additional hard parses which were
consuming significant database time.
Common causes of environment mismatch are session NLS settings, SQL trace
settings and optimizer parameters.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .55 active sessions, 2.73% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Look for top reason for cursor environment mismatch in
      V$SQL_SHARED_CURSOR.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Hard parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is 1.38 active sessions, 6.88% of total activity.

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Wait class "Application" was not consuming significant database time.
Wait class "Configuration" was not consuming significant database time.
CPU was not a bottleneck for the instance.
Wait class "Network" was not consuming significant database time.

Finding 6: Shared Pool Latches
Impact is .63 active sessions, 5.7% of total activity.
------------------------------------------------------
Contention for latches related to the shared pool was consuming significant
database time.
Waits for "latch: shared pool" amounted to 2% of database time.
Waits for "cursor: pin S wait on X" amounted to 1% of database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .63 active sessions, 5.7% of total activity.
   -----------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the cause for latch contention using the given blocking
      sessions or modules.
   Rationale
      The session with ID 2303 and serial number 27026 in instance number 1
      was the blocking session responsible for 21% of this recommendation's
      benefit.
   Rationale
      The session with ID 8782 and serial number 60080 in instance number 1
      was the blocking session responsible for 20% of this recommendation's
      benefit.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Wait class "Concurrency" was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is .75 active sessions, 6.73% of total activity.


Finding 7: Hard Parse Due to Invalidations
Impact is .54 active sessions, 4.87% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
Cursors were getting invalidated due to DDL operations. This resulted in
additional hard parses which were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .54 active sessions, 4.87% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate appropriateness of DDL operations.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Hard parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is 1.2 active sessions, 10.8% of total activity.


Finding 8: Hard Parse Due to Sharing Criteria
Impact is .47 active sessions, 4.21% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
SQL statements with the same text were not shared because of cursor
environment mismatch. This resulted in additional hard parses which were
consuming significant database time.
Common causes of environment mismatch are session NLS settings, SQL trace
settings and optimizer parameters.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .47 active sessions, 4.21% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Look for top reason for cursor environment mismatch in
      V$SQL_SHARED_CURSOR.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Hard parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is 1.2 active sessions, 10.8% of total activity.


Finding 9: Unusual "User I/O" Wait Event
Impact is .4 active sessions, 3.61% of total activity.
------------------------------------------------------
Wait event "Disk file operations I/O" in wait class "User I/O" was consuming
significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .4 active sessions, 3.61% of total activity.
   -----------------------------------------------------------------

      to Oracle's "Database Reference" for the description of this wait event.

      Service "SYS$USERS".

   ------------------------------------------------------------------

      Module "oracle@ambaddb1".

   Recommendation 4: Application Analysis

   ------------------------------------------------------------------

Finding 4: PL/SQL Execution
Impact is .72 active sessions, 9.96% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
PL/SQL execution consumed significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: SQL Tuning
   Estimated benefit is .69 active sessions, 9.63% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Tune the entry point PL/SQL
      "MAYRGBSP.PKG_CBVER02_FFDRENEW.POST_FDRENTRAN" of type "PACKAGE" and ID
      19650597. Refer to the PL/SQL documentation for addition information.
   Rationale
      2512 seconds spent in executing PL/SQL
      "MAYRGBSP.PKG_FDINVSCHEDULE.GENERATE_FDINVSCH" of type "PACKAGE" and ID
      19652035.

   Recommendation 2: SQL Tuning
   Estimated benefit is .02 active sessions, .32% of total activity.
   -----------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Tune the entry point PL/SQL "KBPMJ.PKG_COMMON_PROC.PROC_SETENV" of type
      "PACKAGE" and ID 88942. Refer to the PL/SQL documentation for addition
      information.


Finding 5: Soft Parse
Impact is .62 active sessions, 8.55% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
Soft parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .62 active sessions, 8.55% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic to keep open the frequently used cursors.
      Note that cursors are closed by both cursor close calls and session
      disconnects.

   Recommendation 2: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is .62 active sessions, 8.55% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Consider increasing the session cursor cache size by increasing the
      value of parameter "session_cached_cursors".
   Rationale
      The value of parameter "session_cached_cursors" was "1000" during the
      analysis period.


Finding 6: Commits and Rollbacks
Impact is .45 active sessions, 6.31% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
Waits on event "log file sync" while performing COMMIT and ROLLBACK operations
were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Host Configuration
   Estimated benefit is .45 active sessions, 6.31% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the possibility of improving the performance of I/O to the
      online redo log files.
   Rationale
      The average size of writes to the online redo log files was 48 K and the
      average time per write was 0 milliseconds.
   Rationale
      The total I/O throughput on redo log files was 12 M per second for reads
      and 25 M per second for writes.
   Rationale
      The redo log I/O throughput was divided as follows: 0% by RMAN and
      recovery, 66% by Log Writer, 0% by Archiver, 0% by Streams AQ and 33% by
      all other activity.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Wait class "Commit" was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is .45 active sessions, 6.31% of total activity.


Finding 7: Undersized SGA
Impact is .41 active sessions, 5.69% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
The SGA was inadequately sized, causing additional I/O or hard parses.
The value of parameter "sga_target" was "143360 M" during the analysis period.

   Recommendation 1: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is .12 active sessions, 1.62% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Increase the size of the SGA by setting the parameter "sga_target" to
      152320 M.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Wait class "User I/O" was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is 1.15 active sessions, 15.99% of total activity.
      Hard parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is .65 active sessions, 9.06% of total activity.


Finding 8: Hard Parse Due to Invalidations
Impact is .39 active sessions, 5.41% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
Cursors were getting invalidated due to DDL operations. This resulted in
additional hard parses which were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .39 active sessions, 5.41% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate appropriateness of DDL operations.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Hard parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is .65 active sessions, 9.06% of total activity.


Finding 9: Hard Parse Due to Sharing Criteria
Impact is .15 active sessions, 2.14% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
SQL statements with the same text were not shared because of cursor
environment mismatch. This resulted in additional hard parses which were
consuming significant database time.
Common causes of environment mismatch are session NLS settings, SQL trace
settings and optimizer parameters.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .15 active sessions, 2.14% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Look for top reason for cursor environment mismatch in
      V$SQL_SHARED_CURSOR.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Hard parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is .65 active sessions, 9.06% of total activity.
